note: Draft vectors for LIP-0020. Keys are published BIP-340 test keys, never real keys. Contract identifiers, the name and the name transaction are placeholders. Where an entry gives `hex`, the octets are the vector and the text only shows them. Signatures are made by the default signing algorithm of BIP-340 with 32 zero octets of auxiliary randomness unless `aux_rand` says otherwise. Every refused vector outside a group named `compound` holds one defect and names a valid neighbour of the same stage that differs from it in that defect, in its octets or in its context. A vector of a `compound` group holds several defects on purpose and lists them; it has no neighbour. No checker for these vectors is in this repository.

stages.checks: W1.1 to W1.6 on octets, in the order of W9.2. The largest size is 1048576 octets in this group, which no vector reaches.
W2.3 on the content of a string, for the stated bound.

The entries of `primitives` are arithmetic on given octets under a given type string: a tagged hash, a signature over it, two SHA-256 values. The octets hold `type` alone, or `type` and `note`. For five of the seven types no schema exists, so these octets are no valid object of any type: a reader of grants refuses them as WIRE_TYPE today and will refuse them as WIRE_MEMBER once the grant has members. A checker recomputes the values and parses no grant.
The pipeline of a signed object (section 9) on the signed form of an assent, whose schema is complete; for `bindings`, W7.2 with the stated context.

The pipeline of a Nostr event (section 9) on a consent event, with the stated context. For a recipient by name the context states the facts that the verifier's node would supply about the evidence output.

What an issuer decides before it signs a grant (W7.6, W7.8, W7.9), from the event and the stated context: its clock, the event ids that it has recorded as consumed and, for a recipient by name, the facts of its snapshot. `sign` means that no rule refuses.

For `valid` and `invalid`: the preparation, the commitment and the frame from stated inputs (W8.2 to W8.6). The grant is given as three values of a stand-in from `primitives`, and no grant is parsed. For `stored` and `compound`: the pipeline of an unsigned payload on stored octets of a preparation.

rules.title: each integer member has one form
rules.not_covered: A member in the string form with a number in its place: no complete type has a member in the string form.

rules.title: exact arithmetic
rules.not_covered: Addition and multiplication at a bound: no rule of LIP-0020 computes with an integer. canon-i-29 shows only that a reader decides on the digits.

rules.title: a closed list of members at every depth
the key of the place
rules.not_covered: A key of the place that comes from a pin and is no point of the curve: the one complete signed type, the assent, names its own key.

rules.title: recomputed, never trusted
rules.not_covered: A reference from one object to another, such as a parent in a child: no complete type holds one. id-02 to id-04 compare stated values.

rules.title: the consent event
rules.not_covered: The largest size of the event, 2048 octets: an event above it and an event in another spelling refuse under the same code.

rules.title: consent of a recipient by key
consent of a recipient by name
rules.not_covered: The reads on a node. The cases give the facts that a node would supply and test the decision that follows from them.

rules.title: a later change of the channel key
the time and the age of a consent
the evidence outpoint and the mode
the class of the place selects the pipeline

valid.claim: The empty object.
One member.
Nested objects and arrays; an array keeps its order.
Names in code unit order: uppercase letters, then the underscore, then lowercase letters.
Names ordered by UTF-16 code units: U+1F600, whose first code unit is D83D, stands before U+FB33. Order by code points or by UTF-8 octets would put U+FB33 first.
Strings outside ASCII, and a URL, are written literally in UTF-8: no escape for a slash, an ampersand or an angle bracket.
The two escapes: a quotation mark and a backslash.
U+007F and U+2028 are written literally; neither is below U+0020.
The largest integer of the number form, and zero.

Sixteen levels of nesting, the largest depth.
A URL with slashes.
A letter outside ASCII, written literally.
A character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, written literally in four octets.
A plain string.

The same value with an exponent.
One above the largest integer of the number form.

compound.claim: A null and a negative number. Within W1.4 a null is reported before a number.
The same two defects in the other order of the octets. The order of the rules decides, not the position.

A repeated name, a null and an escaped line feed.
A fraction and an unpaired surrogate.

integers.note: The string form of W2.3, for a member whose bound is 2^64 - 1. Each entry is the content of the JSON string. No complete type of LIP-0020 has a member in the string form, so these vectors test the grammar and the bound, not a member.

The octets hold `type` alone, or `type` and `note`. For five of the seven types no schema exists, so these octets are no valid object of any type: a reader of grants refuses them as WIRE_TYPE today and will refuse them as WIRE_MEMBER once the grant has members. cross.claim: The same octets under the tag of another type give another digest. A reader never computes this: the tag is the type that the payload states.

descriptive.claim: Two octet strings that differ in one descriptive member. The member is inside the canonical bytes, so the typed digest and the SHA-256 differ.

grant_stand_in.claim: The values that the issuance vectors use for a grant: the typed digest of the octets, a signature over it by the issuer's test key, the SHA-256 of the octets and the SHA-256 of the signed octets.
The same octets signed with other auxiliary randomness: another signature and another content address, the same identifier.

The name's newest operation is not confirmed.
The name is expired at the snapshot.
The name's current output is held by another key than the owner key that the grant would sign.
